scope: Unadopted shared indexed 3D head prototype; no production or whole-appearance acceptance

historicalExecutedTestSource.qualification: Executed and read before parent repair; current test and prototype may now differ. Verdict binds the frozen original source.

findings.issue: The clamped face factor is used only as a boolean. Full facial relief is added for every positive factor, then drops abruptly to zero across cos(angle)=0. The supposedly continuous shared head skin therefore has an angular discontinuity at both profile boundaries.
findings.reproduction: Default shaved appearance, y=166, angle=PI/2 plus/minus 1e-8: point distance 1.6867652997065252. The discrepancy persists at other vertical samples and the opposite profile boundary.
findings.requiredCorrection: Apply a continuous, preferably C1, angular weight to the complete relief and independently test boundary values and tangents on both sides. Existing authored breadth-station tangent tests do not test this boundary.
findings.disposition: Parent accepted and subsequently repaired separately. This R1 does not approve the forthcoming repair.

independentChecks.qualification: Independent red probe against frozen original; confirms defect rather than desired continuity
Independent bounded mesh construction, not device or browser performance acceptance

imageBinding: These canonical capture copies retain the original reviewed pixels and all eight hashes match frozen primary. Live output/playwright images were subsequently regenerated for repair and are excluded from this R1.
visualAssessment: Shared profile volume and attached neck improve the initial prototype. Skin remains low-detail and mannequin-like, hair resembles solid caps, and eyes/beard remain simplified shader patterns. Images do not establish complete adult-person art quality or all saved-trait fidelity.

primaryExecutionOnly.qualification: Primary execution attributed; reviewer did not rerun browser

verifiedArchitecture: Front and profile cameras reuse indexed person geometry; pigment changes preserve geometry, normals and topology in tested cases.

Primary open/closed/open blink checks restore pixels and retain the mesh for six people.
limits: One indexed mesh contains intersecting/separate ears, neck, hair and garment parts; this is not evidence of a wholly connected or watertight anatomy mesh.
Timing is one local synchronous observation, not mobile/UI performance validation; indexing and tessellation both changed.
Saved identity/frame purity is bounded to tested DTOs. All hair, gray, dye, part, grooming and facial traits are not yet integrated.
No actual roster/dossier/moving-body/save adoption, context-loss/lifecycle/cache/fallback or full malformed-input acceptance.
